decisions.reason: S-D6 puts advanced options in an on-screen menu and the notes list the audio, image and channel settings.
S-D5 targets the age range sixteen to forty.
No summary part says the remote is for the TV only.
S-D4 and S-D10 keep the corporate logo on the remote.
S-D8 and S-A1 place the screen at the bottom, conflicting with the top placement that S-D9 and the tldr also state.
S-D9 and the tldr place the microphone on top.
The layout notes put LED lights under the buttons.
The layout notes say the LEDs show which buttons are active for the current function.

action_items.reason: S-A5 reorganises documents; no summary part mentions writing minutes.
S-A1 has the User Interface Designer draw the remote control layout.
S-A7 has the User Interface Designer design the menu layout, and the menu is on the screen per S-D6.
S-A3 gives the working design, including how components interact, to the User Interface Designer instead of the Industrial Designer.
